The '''2021–22 season''' was [[Chelsea F.C.|Chelsea Football Club]]'s [[List of Chelsea F.C. seasons|116th year in existence]] and 33rd consecutive season in the top flight of [[Football in England|English football]]. In addition to the [[2021–22 Premier League|domestic league]], Chelsea participated in this season's editions of the [[2021–22 FA Cup|FA Cup]], [[2021–22 EFL Cup|EFL Cup]], [[2021–22 UEFA Champions League|UEFA Champions League]], [[2021 UEFA Super Cup|UEFA Super Cup]] and [[2021 FIFA Club World Cup|FIFA Club World Cup]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=History|url=https://www.chelseafc.com/en/about-chelsea/history|website=chelseafc.com|date=1 July 2020}}</ref> The season covered the period from 1 July 2021 to 30 June 2022.

Chelsea finished the 2021–22 season with two trophies out of a possible six, winning the UEFA Super Cup and FIFA Club World Cup. The club's victory in the latter competition was significant as it not only confirmed Chelsea as [[List of world champion football clubs|World Champions]] for the first time, but also clinched the only outstanding piece of silverware that the club had not previously won. Upon adding the title to the club's honours, Chelsea joined an exclusive list of [[AFC Ajax|Ajax]], [[FC Bayern Munich|Bayern Munich]], [[Juventus FC|Juventus]] and [[Manchester United F.C.|Manchester United]] as the five clubs that have won every single major honour in European and international football.

On the domestic front, Chelsea reached the finals of both cup competitions, defeated only on penalties by [[Liverpool F.C.|Liverpool]] after goalless draws on both occasions. In the Premier League, Chelsea began the season strongly and led the title race from October to early December. However, inconsistent form through December and January blunted their title challenge, with the Blues eventually finishing a distant third. In the Champions League, their title defence ended with a quarter-final elimination at the hands of eventual [[2022 UEFA Champions League Final|winners]] [[Real Madrid CF|Real Madrid]].

== Season summary ==
=== August ===
On 11 August 2021, Chelsea started off the season by beating [[Villarreal CF|Villarreal]] to win the [[2021 UEFA Super Cup]]. [[Hakim Ziyech]] opened the scoring in the 27th minute before [[Gerard Moreno]] scored in the 73rd minute to equalise; after extra time the score remained 1–1. In the final minute of the match, [[Thomas Tuchel]] made the decision to replace goalkeeper [[Édouard Mendy]] with [[Kepa Arrizabalaga]]. Chelsea went on to win 6–5 on penalties, with Arrizabalaga making the decisive save against [[Raúl Albiol]].<ref>{{Cite web|date=2021-08-11|title=Kepa the hero as Chelsea beat Villarreal on penalties to win Uefa Super Cup|url=http://www.theguardian.com/football/2021/aug/11/chelsea-villarreal-super-cup-final-match-report|access-date=2021-09-07|website=The Guardian|language=en}}</ref> Following the match, Thomas Tuchel stated: "We were well-prepared. We had a statistic that Kepa is the best in terms of saving penalties. The analysts showed me the data and then we spoke with the players [explaining] that this can happen in knockout games."<ref>{{Cite web|date=2021-08-11|title=Chelsea 1-1 Villarreal (pens: 6-5): Kepa edges Blues to silverware|url=https://www.uefa.com/uefasupercup/news/026c-12f9fcd5041f-0109d61295b7-1000--chelsea-1-1-villarreal-pens-6-5-kepa-edges-blues-to-silverware/|access-date=2021-09-07|website=[[UEFA]]|language=en}}</ref> It was the second time that Chelsea had won the trophy, the first win being in [[1998 UEFA Super Cup|1998]], and the third time that the club was involved in a penalty shoot-out in the competition.<ref name=UEFASC>{{cite web|url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2021/aug/11/chelsea-villarreal-super-cup-final-match-report|title=Kepa the hero as Chelsea beat Villarreal on penalties to win UEFA Super Cup|website=The Guardian|date=11 August 2021}}</ref>

The following day, Chelsea announced that [[Romelu Lukaku]] had re-signed for the club seven years after leaving for a reported club record fee of £97.5 million.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.chelseafc.com/en/news/2021/08/12/romelu-lukaku-comes-home/|title=Romelu Lukaku comes home|website=Chelsea F.C.|access-date=12 August 2021}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|title=Chelsea re-sign Lukaku for club record £97.5m|language=en-GB|work=BBC Sport|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/58111490|access-date=2021-08-12}}</ref> Although initial offers were turned down by [[Inter Milan]], Chelsea's third offer for Lukaku was accepted. "I only realised that Chelsea was serious at the third offer," Lukaku stated. "It went to €110m, and I knew, this is truly serious." He continued, "If they ask me, why would I say no? Everyone knows what Chelsea means to me."<ref>{{Cite web|title='I WAS IN A DEEP HOLE AT MAN UTD' - ROMELU LUKAKU ADMITS HE WOULD HAVE ONLY LEFT INTER MILAN FOR CHELSEA|url=https://www.eurosport.com/geoblocking.shtml|url-status=live|access-date=2021-09-07|website=www.eurosport.com|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200110133019/https://www.eurosport.com/geoblocking.shtml |archive-date=10 January 2020 }}</ref>

Chelsea began the Premier League season with two consecutive wins in [[London derbies]], first at home against [[Crystal Palace F.C.|Crystal Palace]] and then at the [[Emirates Stadium]] against [[Arsenal F.C.|Arsenal]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|title=Chelsea v Crystal Palace, 2021/22 |url=https://www.premierleague.com/match/66344|access-date=2021-09-07|website=www.premierleague.com|language=en}}</ref><ref name=":1">{{Cite web|title=Arsenal v Chelsea, 2021/22 |url=https://www.premierleague.com/match/66352|access-date=2021-09-07|website=www.premierleague.com|language=en}}</ref> In the former, Premier League debutant [[Trevoh Chalobah]] scored the final goal in a 3–0 win with a low right-footed shot from well outside the penalty area.<ref name=":0" /> In the latter, new signing [[Romelu Lukaku]] scored the opening goal in a 2–0 win on his second debut for the club.<ref name=":1" />

On 28 August, Chelsea travelled to [[Anfield]] to take on [[Liverpool F.C.|Liverpool]] in a match that was billed as an early test for two title contenders.<ref>{{Cite web|date=2021-08-27|title=Liverpool vs Chelsea: Lineups, prediction, team news, odds, how to watch|url=https://soccer.nbcsports.com/2021/08/27/liverpool-vs-chelsea-lineups-prediction-team-news-odds-how-to-watch/|access-date=2021-09-07|website= NBC Sports|language=en-US}}</ref> [[Kai Havertz]] opened the scoring off a corner kick with a looping near-post header that spiraled over goalkeeper [[Alisson]].<ref name="Liverpool v Chelsea, 2021/22 | Premier League" /> In the first half stoppage time, [[Reece James (footballer, born 1999)|Reece James]] was sent off after referee [[Anthony Taylor (referee)|Anthony Taylor]] consulted the [[Video assistant referee|VAR]] and adjudged that James had used his arm to prevent a goal. [[Mohammed Salah]] scored the ensuing penalty despite furious protests from Chelsea players. In the second half, Chelsea defended deeply and compactly and the match finished 1–1.<ref name="Liverpool v Chelsea, 2021/22 | Premier League">{{Cite web|title=Liverpool v Chelsea, 2021/22 |url=https://www.premierleague.com/match/66365|access-date=2021-09-07|website=www.premierleague.com|language=en}}</ref>

On 31 August, transfer deadline day, Chelsea signed [[Saúl Ñíguez|Saúl]] from [[Atlético Madrid]] on a season-long loan with an option to buy at the end of the season.<ref name=":2" /> The future fee is reported to be €40 million.<ref>{{Cite magazine|last=Emms|first=Nick|title=Report: Saul Niguez's Potential Option to Buy in Chelsea Loan Move Revealed|url=https://www.si.com/soccer/chelsea/transfer-news/report-saul-niguez-offered-to-chelsea-on-loan-with-34m-40m-option-to-buy|access-date=2021-11-01|magazine=Sports Illustrated|date=24 August 2021 |language=en}}</ref> Throughout the transfer window, Chelsea were linked with a move for [[Sevilla FC|Sevilla]] centre-back [[Jules Koundé]], although it never materialized.<ref>{{Cite magazine|last=Emms|first=Nick|title=Report: Why Chelsea Pulled Out of Jules Kounde Transfer|url=https://www.si.com/soccer/chelsea/transfer-news/report-why-chelsea-pulled-out-of-jules-kounde-transfer|access-date=2021-09-07|magazine=Sports Illustrated|date=31 August 2021 |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|last=Pasztor|first=David|date=2021-09-05|title=Lopetegui expects Koundé to play key role for Sevilla after Chelsea transfer failure|url=https://weaintgotnohistory.sbnation.com/chelsea-fc-transfer-rumours-news/2021/9/5/22658473/lopetegui-expects-kounde-to-play-key-role-for-sevilla-after-chelsea-transfer-failure|access-date=2021-09-07|website=We Ain't Got No History|language=en}}</ref> The transfer window also saw several notable departures, including [[Olivier Giroud]], [[Tammy Abraham]], and [[Kurt Zouma]].<ref name=":3" /><ref name=":4" /><ref name=":5" /> Furthermore, Chelsea sold several promising youth academy products, including [[Marc Guéhi]], [[Tino Livramento]], and [[Ike Ugbo]].<ref name=":6" /><ref name=":7" /><ref name=":8" />

[[Marcos Alonso (footballer, born 1990)|Marcos Alonso]] was nominated for the Premier League Player of the Month award in August, which was eventually given to West Ham's [[Michail Antonio]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=August 2021's EA SPORTS Player of the Month nominees|url=http://www.premierleague.com/news/2233838|access-date=2021-11-04|website=www.premierleague.com|date=5 September 2021 |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|title=Antonio named August 2021 EA SPORTS Player of the Month|language=en|url=https://www.premierleague.com/news/2245539|access-date=2021-11-04}}</ref> Thomas Tuchel was also nominated for Premier League Manager of the Month, but it was awarded to Tottenham's [[Nuno Espírito Santo]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=August 2021's Barclays Manager of the Month shortlist|url=http://www.premierleague.com/news/2233840|access-date=2021-11-04|website=www.premierleague.com|date=5 September 2021 |language=en}}</ref><ref name=":11">{{Cite web|title=Premier League Awards - Player, Manager & Goal of the Month|url=https://www.premierleague.com/stats/awards|access-date=2021-11-04|website=www.premierleague.com|language=en}}</ref>

=== September ===
Chelsea started September with back-to-back 3–0 wins against [[Aston Villa F.C.|Aston Villa]] and [[Tottenham Hotspur F.C.|Tottenham Hotspur]] in the Premier League and a 1–0 win against Zenit in the Champions League.<ref name=":9">{{Cite web|title=Chelsea v Aston Villa, 2021/22|url=https://www.premierleague.com/match/66374|access-date=2021-09-22|website=www.premierleague.com|language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=Spurs v Chelsea, 2021/22 |url=https://www.premierleague.com/match/66389|access-date=2021-09-22|website=www.premierleague.com|language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=Chelsea-Zenit |url=https://www.uefa.com/uefachampionsleague/match/2032702--chelsea-vs-zenit/|access-date=2021-09-22|website=[[UEFA]]|language=en}}</ref> After five matchdays in the Premier League, Chelsea and Liverpool coincidentally shared identical records, with Chelsea ahead based on the away goals head-to-head tiebreaker following their meeting on Matchday 3.<ref>{{Cite news|last=Edgar|first=Bill|title=Game in numbers: Chelsea and Liverpool complete historic five-match run|newspaper=[[The Times]] |language=en|url=https://www.thetimes.com/sport/football/article/game-in-numbers-chelsea-and-liverpool-complete-historic-five-match-run-0bjx9lk7x|access-date=2021-09-22|issn=0140-0460}}</ref> On 22 September, Chelsea faced Aston Villa again in the EFL Cup, winning 4–3 on penalties after a 1–1 draw.<ref name=":10">{{Cite news|title=Chelsea beat Villa in EFL Cup shootout|language=en-GB|work=BBC Sport|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/58566909|access-date=2021-09-23}}</ref> Kepa Arrizabalaga made a decisive save against a spot kick from [[Marvelous Nakamba]], which led him to become Chelsea's most successful goalkeeper at saving penalties during shootouts, passing [[Petr Čech]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Kepa breaks Chelsea penalty shoot-out record |url=https://www.chelseafc.com/en/news/2021/09/23/kepa-breaks-chelsea-penalty-shoot-out-record|access-date=2021-09-25|website=ChelseaFC}}</ref> Both matches against Aston Villa saw debuts, first in the Premier League for [[Saúl Ñíguez|Saúl]] and in the EFL Cup for [[Malang Sarr]].<ref name=":9" /><ref name=":10" />

On 25 September, Chelsea faced off against [[Manchester City F.C.|Manchester City]] at Stamford Bridge. Manchester City dominated possession and employed a high press throughout the match, with [[Gabriel Jesus]] scoring the game's only goal in the 53rd minute. The 1–0 defeat was Chelsea's first loss of the season.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Chelsea v Man City, 2021/22 |url=https://www.premierleague.com/match/66394|access-date=2021-09-25|website=www.premierleague.com|language=en}}</ref> Following the match, Thomas Tuchel stated "The performance was not complex enough. Overall, simply, we were not at our best level."<ref>{{Cite web|title=Chelsea vs. Manchester City - Football Match Report - September 25, 2021 - ESPN|url=https://www.espn.com/soccer/report/_/gameId/605983|access-date=2021-09-25|website=ESPN.com|language=en}}</ref> It was the first time that Chelsea were beaten by [[Manchester City F.C.|Manchester City]] under Tuchel, with [[Pep Guardiola]] winning for the first time after three consecutive defeats in the [[2020–21 Chelsea F.C. season|previous season]], including in the [[2021 Champions League Final|Champions League Final]].<ref>{{Cite news|title=Man City end Chelsea's unbeaten start|language=en-GB|work=BBC Sport|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/58606479|access-date=2021-09-25}}</ref>

On 29 September, Chelsea suffered their first Champions League defeat of the season, losing 0–1 to [[Juventus FC|Juventus]] in Turin. [[Federico Chiesa]] scored the game's only goal just after halftime. Although Chelsea enjoyed a majority of possession in the game, Juventus defended deeply and created several chances on the counter-attack.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Juventus-Chelsea |url=https://www.uefa.com/uefachampionsleague/match/2032734--juventus-vs-chelsea/?iv=true|access-date=2021-10-10|website=[[UEFA]]|language=en}}</ref> Chelsea ended the month of September with only three goals conceded in six matches. Chelsea's successful defensive performances led to [[Antonio Rüdiger]] being nominated for Premier League Player of the Month, though it was eventually awarded to [[Cristiano Ronaldo]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=September 2021's EA Sports Player of the Month shortlist|url=http://www.premierleague.com/news/2272843|access-date=2021-11-04|website=www.premierleague.com|date=2 October 2021 |language=en}}</ref><ref name=":11" />

=== October ===

Chelsea began October with a 3–1 win against Southampton. After an early goal from Trevoh Chalobah, [[James Ward-Prowse]] equalised from the penalty spot before he was sent off in the 77th minute. Chelsea rallied to win with two late goals from [[Timo Werner]] and [[Ben Chilwell]], who scored with a close-range left-footed volley in his first start in the Premier League during the season.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Chelsea v Southampton, 2021/22 |url=https://www.premierleague.com/match/66404|access-date=2021-10-10|website=www.premierleague.com|language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=Chilwell on patience, perspective and a good if surprising goal |url=https://www.chelseafc.com/en/news/2021/10/04/chilwell-on-patience--perspective-and-a-good-but-surprising-goal|access-date=2021-10-10|website=ChelseaFC}}</ref> On 16 October, Chelsea beat [[Brentford F.C.|Brentford]] 1–0 in the first iteration of this [[West London derby]] in the modern Premier League era. Chilwell scored for the second consecutive game, while Mendy made four crucial saves to preserve a clean sheet.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Brentford v Chelsea, 2021/22 |url=https://www.premierleague.com/match/66414|access-date=2021-10-18|website=www.premierleague.com|language=en}}</ref> Chelsea played their third Champions League group stage match on 20 October against [[Malmö FF|Malmö]], winning 4–0. [[Jorginho (footballer, born December 1991)|Jorginho]] scored two penalties and [[Andreas Christensen]] scored his first career goal for Chelsea after 137 appearances. However, both Romelu Lukaku and Timo Werner were injured during the match.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Chelsea-Malmö |url=https://www.uefa.com/uefachampionsleague/match/2032711--chelsea-vs-malmo/?iv=true|access-date=2021-10-27|website=[[UEFA]]|language=en}}</ref>

On 23 October, Chelsea beat [[Norwich City F.C.|Norwich City]] 7–0 in the Premier League with [[Mason Mount]] scoring his first ever senior hat-trick. The 7–0 win was the joint second-highest scoreline in Chelsea's Premier League history.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Chelsea v Norwich, 2021/22|url=https://www.premierleague.com/match/66425|access-date=2021-10-28|website=www.premierleague.com|language=en|archive-date=23 August 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210823182038/https://www.premierleague.com/match/66425|url-status=dead}}</ref> Ben Chilwell scored for the fourth consecutive Premier League match, becoming the first Chelsea player to do so since [[Eden Hazard]].<ref>{{Citation|title=Chelsea 7-0 Norwich {{!}} Cobham's Finest Score 7 at the Bridge!| date=23 October 2021 |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=GlTsktEX8jw|language=en|access-date=2021-10-27}}</ref> Goals from [[Callum Hudson-Odoi]] and Reece James meant that 17 different players had scored for Chelsea in all competitions.<ref>{{Cite magazine|last=Hemming|first=Jago|title=Comment: Chelsea's Goalscoring Versatility Softens Romelu Lukaku Blow|url=https://www.si.com/soccer/chelsea/fan-opinions/comment-chelseas-goal-scoring-versatility-softens-romelu-lukaku-blow|access-date=2021-10-28|magazine=Sports Illustrated|date=24 October 2021 |language=en}}</ref> On 26 October, Chelsea took on Southampton at home in the EFL Cup round of 16. Kai Havertz and [[Ché Adams]] scored the only goals of the game, with Chelsea going on to win 4–3 on penalties.<ref>{{Cite news|title=Chelsea into League Cup quarter-finals|language=en-GB|work=BBC Sport|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/58963258|access-date=2021-10-28}}</ref> Chelsea ended the month of October with a 3–0 win against [[Newcastle United F.C.|Newcastle United]] at [[St James' Park|St. James' Park]]. After a goalless first half, Reece James scored two goals from the far-right corner of the [[penalty area]], the first of which was a left-footed half-volley, ending the Premier League month of top of the league.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Newcastle v Chelsea, 2021/22 |url=https://www.premierleague.com/match/66437|access-date=2021-11-01|website=www.premierleague.com|language=en}}</ref>

Chelsea ended the month of October with a 1–0 win away against Malmö, with Hakim Ziyech scoring the winner.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Malmö-Chelsea|url=https://www.uefa.com/uefachampionsleague/match/2032655--malmo-vs-chelsea/|access-date=2021-11-04|website=[[UEFA]]|language=en}}</ref> Ben Chilwell was nominated for Premier League Player of the Month, and Thomas Tuchel was nominated for Premier League Manager of the Month for the second time, eventually going on to win the award.<ref name="premierleague.com">{{Cite web|title=Vote for October's EA SPORTS Player of the Month|url=http://www.premierleague.com/news/2325837|access-date=2021-11-04|website=www.premierleague.com|language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=Tuchel named October 2021 Barclays Manager of the Month|url=http://www.premierleague.com/news/2346152|access-date=2021-12-30|website=www.premierleague.com|date=12 November 2021 |language=en}}</ref>

=== November ===

November began with Trevoh Chalobah signing a contract extension through 2026. "It's quite surreal," Chalobah said. "It's a dream for me to sign a new long-term contract for my boyhood club and hopefully the dream continues. It's been an unbelievable start to the season and something I never expected but it just shows that the hard work I've put in and going out on loans has paid off."<ref>{{Cite web|title=Chalobah agrees new long-term Chelsea deal |url=https://www.chelseafc.com/en/news/2021/11/04/chalobah-agrees-new-long-term-chelsea-deal|access-date=2021-11-05|website=ChelseaFC}}</ref>

On 6 November, Chelsea drew [[Burnley F.C.|Burnley]] 1–1, with Kai Havertz scoring the opening goal before [[Matěj Vydra]] equalised.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Chelsea v Burnley, 2021/22 |url=https://www.premierleague.com/match/66445|access-date=2021-11-11|website=www.premierleague.com|language=en}}</ref> It was only the third time of the season that Chelsea dropped points in the Premier League. Entering into the international break, Chelsea were in first place in the Premier League, three points clear of second place Manchester City.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Premier League Table, Form Guide & Season Archives|url=https://www.premierleague.com/tables?co=1&se=418&ha=-1|access-date=2021-11-11|website=www.premierleague.com|language=en}}</ref> Throughout the month of November, Chelsea was reported to be in negotiations with Antonio Rüdiger and Andreas Christensen over new contracts. Speaking about the negotiations, Thomas Tuchel said, "I feel the situation is calm here inside and from here we go." He went on, "You can end up in situations like this but the situations are handled from all sides very carefully, professionally and mature."<ref>{{Cite web|last=Pasztor|first=David|date=2021-11-19|title=Tuchel still calm and hopeful of new Rüdiger, Christensen contracts|url=https://weaintgotnohistory.sbnation.com/2021/11/19/22791446/tuchel-still-calm-and-hopeful-of-new-rudiger-christensen-contracts|access-date=2021-12-03|website=We Ain't Got No History|language=en}}</ref>

Chelsea returned from the international break on 20 November to beat [[Leicester City F.C.|Leicester City]] 3–0 at the [[King Power Stadium]]. [[N'Golo Kanté]] scored a long-range goal from outside of the penalty area against his former club and substitute [[Christian Pulisic]] scored after returning from a lengthy ankle injury.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Leicester v Chelsea, 2021/22|url=https://www.premierleague.com/match/66454|access-date=2021-12-03|website=www.premierleague.com|language=en|archive-date=4 April 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230404194054/https://www.premierleague.com/match/66454|url-status=dead}}</ref>

On 24 November, Chelsea took on Juventus in a crucial Champions League group stage match. Heading into Matchday 5, Chelsea were second in Group H, three points behind the Italian side after losing in Turin on Matchday 2. Chelsea needed to win by a margin of two goals or more to move to the top of the group leading into the final matchday due to Juventus' superior goal difference. From the opening whistle, Chelsea employed an extremely attacking approach, with the five defenders playing an extremely high line and the forwards aggressively pressuring the ball in Juventus' half. Trevoh Chalobah scored the game's opener off a corner kick to put Chelsea 1–0 up. Five minutes later, Thiago Silva cleared a shot from former Chelsea player [[Álvaro Morata]] off the line with a dramatic overhead kick to preserve the one-goal advantage at the break. In the second half, Chelsea scored two goals in two minutes from Reece James and Callum Hudson-Odoi before Timo Werner made it 4–0 in stoppage time.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Chelsea-Juventus|url=https://www.uefa.com/uefachampionsleague/match/2032662--chelsea-vs-juventus/?iv=true|access-date=2021-12-03|website=[[UEFA]]|language=en}}</ref> The win was Chelsea's largest ever in a competitive fixture against Juventus and guaranteed their progression to the knockout rounds of the Champions League.<ref>{{Cite web|last=LiveScore|first=SofaScore com|title=Chelsea vs Juventus live score, H2H and lineups |url=https://www.sofascore.com/chelsea-juventus/NsMdb|access-date=2021-12-03|website=www.sofascore.com|language=en}}</ref> However, Ben Chilwell suffered anterior cruciate ligament damage during the match, ruling him out for the rest of the season.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2021-12-28 |title=Sources: Chelsea's Chilwell out for the season |url=https://www.espn.com/soccer/chelsea-engchelsea/story/4557519/chelseas-ben-chilwell-to-miss-rest-of-season-through-injury-sources |access-date=2022-05-09 |website=ESPN.com |language=en}}</ref>

The following Sunday, Chelsea took on Manchester United, who had recently sacked manager [[Ole Gunnar Solskjær]]. Despite having almost two-thirds of the possession, Chelsea could only manage a 1–1 draw. Jorginho's heavy touch allowed [[Jadon Sancho]] to score the game's opener, but he later converted a penalty to level the score line.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Chelsea v Man Utd, 2021/22 |url=https://www.premierleague.com/match/66466|access-date=2021-12-03|website=www.premierleague.com|language=en}}</ref>

=== December ===

Chelsea began the busy December period with a match against Watford. Players had to leave the pitch for 25 minutes due to a medical incident in the [[Graham Taylor]] Stand at [[Vicarage Road]]. Paramedics rushed onto the pitch about 12 minutes into the game to treat a supporter, who was taken to a local hospital and later reported to be in stable condition.<ref>{{Cite web|last=evan-bartlett|date=2021-12-01|title=Football fan in stable condition 'after suffering heart attack' in Watford vs Chelsea match|url=https://inews.co.uk/sport/football/watford-vs-chelsea-suspended-fan-heart-attack-vicarage-road-medical-emergency-1330616|access-date=2021-12-03|website=inews.co.uk|language=en}}</ref> Chelsea went on to win the game 2–1, courtesy of goals from Mason Mount and Hakim Ziyech.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Watford v Chelsea, 2021/22 |url=https://www.premierleague.com/match/66476|access-date=2021-12-03|website=www.premierleague.com|language=en}}</ref>

Chelsea's third competitive defeat of the season came on December 4 as they travelled to the [[London Stadium]] to take on [[West Ham United F.C.|West Ham]], who sat in fourth place in the Premier League. Chelsea lead twice through goals from Thiago Silva and Mason Mount, but were twice pegged back. In the 87th minute, [[Arthur Masuaku]] scored the game's winner with a cross-come-shot that beat Mendy at his near post. The result meant that Chelsea slipped to third in the Premier League, behind Manchester City and Liverpool, relinquishing the top spot for the first time since Matchday 6.<ref>{{Cite web|title=West Ham v Chelsea, 2021/22|url=https://www.premierleague.com/match/66490|access-date=2021-12-18|website=www.premierleague.com|language=en|archive-date=24 October 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211024073848/https://www.premierleague.com/match/66490|url-status=dead}}</ref> Four days later, Chelsea travelled to [[Saint Petersburg]] to take on [[FC Zenit Saint Petersburg|Zenit]] in the final Champions League group stage match. Going into the final matchday, Chelsea sat atop the group, ahead of Juventus due to their superior head-to-head record. Timo Werner scored an early goal, but by half-time, Zenit had scored twice to give the Russian side the lead. Chelsea battled back in the second half, with Romelu Lukaku equalizing before Werner scored his second in the 85th minute. However, with nearly the last kick of the game, [[Magomed Ozdoyev|Magomed Ozdoev]] made it 3–3 with a half-volley from outside the penalty area. Combined with Juventus' win against Malmö, the result meant that Chelsea would progress as runners-up in Group H.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Zenit-Chelsea|url=https://www.uefa.com/uefachampionsleague/match/2032678--zenit-vs-chelsea/|access-date=2021-12-18|website=[[UEFA]]|language=en}}</ref>

On 11 December, Chelsea were involved in another high-scoring match as they beat [[Leeds United F.C.|Leeds United]] 3–2 courtesy of two penalties from Jorginho, including one in second half stoppage time.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Chelsea v Leeds, 2021/22 |url=https://www.premierleague.com/match/66496|access-date=2021-12-18|website=www.premierleague.com|language=en}}</ref> Chelsea were twice drawn against [[Lille OSC|Lille]] in the Champions League Round of 16, as the results of the initial draw were nullified after technical issues.<ref>{{Cite web|date=2021-12-13|title=UEFA botch Champions League last-16 draw|url=https://www.espn.com/soccer/uefa-champions-league/story/4546776/champions-league-draw-redrawn-after-uefas-man-united-error|access-date=2021-12-18|website=ESPN.com|language=en}}</ref> Five days later, Chelsea returned to action at Stamford Bridge without Timo Werner, Romelu Lukaku, and [[Mateo Kovačić]] due to COVID-19 against an injury-struck Everton. Despite almost 80% possession, Chelsea could only manage a 1–1 draw, as Mason Mount's seventh goal of the season was followed by [[Jarrad Branthwaite]]'s first ever strike in the Premier League.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Chelsea v Everton, 2021/22|url=https://www.premierleague.com/match/66509|access-date=2021-12-18|website=www.premierleague.com|language=en}}</ref> On 22 December, Chelsea played out a scoreless draw at [[Molineux Stadium]] against [[Wolverhampton Wanderers F.C.|Wolverhampton Wanderers]] before beating Brentford 2–0 in the EFL Cup quarter-final three days later.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Wolves v Chelsea, 2021/22|url=https://www.premierleague.com/match/66521|access-date=2021-12-23|website=www.premierleague.com|language=en|archive-date=22 October 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211022220318/https://www.premierleague.com/match/66521|url-status=dead}}</ref> Chelsea continued to be missing several key players due to COVID-19; in the match against Brentford, Tuchel handed debuts to academy players [[Harvey Vale]], [[Jude Soonsup-Bell]], and [[Xavier Simons]].<ref>{{Cite news|title=Chelsea beat Brentford to reach semis|language=en-GB|work=BBC Sport|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/59662104|access-date=2021-12-23}}</ref>

On [[Boxing Day]], Chelsea beat Aston Villa 3–1 courtesy of two penalties from Jorginho and a goal from Romelu Lukaku on his return to the squad.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Aston Villa v Chelsea, 2021/22|url=https://www.premierleague.com/match/66522|access-date=2021-12-30|website=www.premierleague.com|language=en|archive-date=26 October 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211026041116/https://www.premierleague.com/match/66522|url-status=dead}}</ref> Three days later, Chelsea could only manage a draw against [[Brighton & Hove Albion F.C.|Brighton]] at Stamford Bridge. Lukaku opened the scoring but Chelsea were pegged back in stoppage time as [[Danny Welbeck]] equalised. The result meant that Chelsea had failed to win consecutive home games since October.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Chelsea v Brighton, 2021/22|url=https://www.premierleague.com/match/66534|access-date=2021-12-30|website=www.premierleague.com|language=en|archive-date=26 October 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211026083930/https://www.premierleague.com/match/66534|url-status=dead}}</ref> Following the match, Tuchel admitted that Chelsea's hopes of winning the Premier League title were slim, in part due to the effects of COVID-19 within the squad, stating "How should we compete in a title race? It would be stupid. I simply don't know what I can expect from my players. Nobody knows it.”<ref>{{Cite web|date=2021-12-29|title=Brighton's Welbeck stuns Chelsea as Tuchel labels title chances as 'stupid'|url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2021/dec/29/chelsea-brighton-premier-league-match-report|access-date=2021-12-30|website=The Guardian|language=en}}</ref> Chelsea ended the calendar year in second, eight points behind league leaders Manchester City and one point ahead of Liverpool, who had a game in hand.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Premier League Table, Form Guide & Season Archives|url=https://www.premierleague.com/tables?co=1&se=418&ha=-1|access-date=2021-12-30|website=www.premierleague.com|language=en}}</ref>

On 31 December, [[Sky Italia]] released an interview with Romelu Lukaku from earlier in the month in which the striker stated that he was unhappy with his lack of game time at Chelsea and eventually wished to return to former club [[Inter Milan]]. "I think the boss has decided to play a different formation but I have to stick at it and get on with it professionally" he stated. "I'm not happy with the situation but it's my job and I mustn't give up." He added, "I hope from the bottom of my heart to go back to Inter and not at the end of my career but when I'm still at a good enough level to win more trophies."<ref>{{Cite web|title=Romelu Lukaku was 'not happy with situation' at Chelsea|url=https://www.skysports.com/football/news/11668/12506438/romelu-lukaku-was-not-happy-with-situation-at-chelsea|access-date=2022-01-06|website=Sky Sports|language=en}}</ref> In another portion of the interview, Lukaku stated "In my opinion, there are three absolute top teams in football — [[Real Madrid CF|Real Madrid]], [[FC Barcelona|Barcelona]] and [[FC Bayern Munich|Bayern Munich]]. Every player dreams of playing for one of these teams one day. So I thought if I ever had that possibility, I would sign a new contract with Inter and then go there...But it didn't happen, so I told myself that there is only one team where I could possibly see myself — Chelsea."<ref>{{Cite web|title=Romelu Lukaku: Chelsea striker says he turned down Manchester City move in 2020 from Inter Milan|url=https://www.skysports.com/football/news/11668/12506740/romelu-lukaku-chelsea-striker-says-he-turned-down-manchester-city-move-in-2020-from-inter-milan|access-date=2022-01-06|website=Sky Sports|language=en}}</ref> The interview caused widespread anger among Chelsea fans.<ref>{{Cite web|author=Matias Grez|title='I am sorry for the upset I have caused': Romelu Lukaku apologizes for incendiary interview|url=https://www.cnn.com/2022/01/05/football/romelu-lukaku-apologizes-for-interview-spt-intl/index.html|access-date=2022-01-06|website=CNN|date=5 January 2022 }}</ref>

=== January ===

Chelsea's first game of the new year came on 2 January at Stamford Bridge. The match saw second-place Chelsea take on third-placed Liverpool, with both teams needing a win to keep pace with league leaders Manchester City. In the press conferences leading up to the match, Tuchel responded to questions about Lukaku's interview by stating "I don't like it because it brings noise that we don't need. It's just not helpful. On the other side, we don't want to make more out of it than it actually is. You know very well how it is - it's very easy to take lines out of context. It's very easy to shorten lines and make headlines, then later realise that it's not so bad and maybe not what he meant." He went on, "But let's be honest that we don't like it."<ref>{{Cite web|title=Romelu Lukaku: Thomas Tuchel admits he is unhappy at Chelsea striker's comments, adding they are 'not helpful'|url=https://www.skysports.com/football/news/11668/12506676/romelu-lukaku-thomas-tuchel-admits-he-is-unhappy-at-chelsea-strikers-comments-adding-they-are-not-helpful|access-date=2022-01-06|website=Sky Sports|language=en}}</ref> Tuchel announced in the pre-match press conference that he decided to drop Lukaku despite the fact that the Belgian had scored in each of the previous two league matches, stating "the thing got too noisy so close to the match, so I decided to protect the preparation of the match, and that's why he's out."<ref>{{Cite web|title=Lukaku dropped by Tuchel from Chelsea squad for Liverpool clash |url=https://www.goal.com/en/news/tuchel-considers-dropping-lukaku-out-of-chelsea-squad/bltaaec554c9cec8351|access-date=2022-01-06|website=www.goal.com}}</ref> Tuchel replaced Lukaku with Kai Havertz playing as a [[False nine|false-nine]]. The match started at a high pace, with chances on both ends. However, Liverpool scored twice in the opening 26 minutes. Just before halftime, Mateo Kovačić struck a volley from outside the penalty area that rifled into the top corner of the net, halving the deficit. Chelsea attacked frenetically before the interval, and in first-half stoppage time, Christian Pulisic controlled N'Golo Kanté's lofted pass and finished powerfully to level the score line at 2 goals for each side. In the second half, both [[Édouard Mendy]] and [[Caoimhín Kelleher|Caoimhin Kelleher]] made crucial saves to keep the score level. The match ended 2–2, with both sides losing ground on Manchester City.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Chelsea v Liverpool, 2021/22|url=https://www.premierleague.com/match/66544|access-date=2022-01-06|website=www.premierleague.com|language=en|archive-date=26 October 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211026035019/https://www.premierleague.com/match/66544|url-status=dead}}</ref>

On 3 January, Chelsea announced that Thiago Silva had extended his contract until 2023.<ref name="Chelsea F.C">{{cite web|url=https://www.chelseafc.com/en/news/2022/01/03/thiago-silva-extends-chelsea-contract-|title=Thiago Silva extends Chelsea contract|publisher=Chelsea F.C.|date=3 January 2022|access-date=4 January 2022}}</ref> The following day, Lukaku issued an official apology to Chelsea fans. "I am sorry for the upset I have caused," he stated. "You guys know the connection I have to the club and I totally understand you guys being upset." He went on, "I should have been much clearer in my message. The interview was about saying goodbye to the Inter fans and it wasn't about trying to disrespect the [Chelsea] fans, my teammates, the club and the manager."<ref>{{Cite web|title="I'm sorry for the upset I have caused." {{!}} Romelu Lukaku - Exclusive Interview|url=https://www.chelseafc.com/en/videos/v/2022/01/04/_i_m-sorry-for-the-upset-i-have-caused----romelu-lukaku---exclus-mb9Xrk2F|access-date=2022-01-06|website=ChelseaFC}}</ref> On 5 January, Chelsea took on Tottenham Hotspur in the League Cup semi-final first leg at Stamford Bridge, with Lukaku returning to the starting lineup. Chelsea won the match 2–0, courtesy of a goal from Kai Havertz and a [[Ben Davies (footballer, born 1993)|Ben Davies]] own-goal, which occurred in bizarre fashion after [[Japhet Tanganga]]'s clearance bounced back off the Welshman's face into the net.<ref>{{Cite news|title=Dominant Chelsea beat Spurs in first leg|language=en-GB|work=BBC Sport|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/59814563|access-date=2022-01-06}}</ref> The following weekend, Chelsea beat [[National League (English football)|National League]] side [[Chesterfield F.C.|Chesterfield]] 5–1 in the [[2021–22 FA Cup#Third round proper|FA Cup third round]] in a match that saw [[Lewis Hall (footballer)|Lewis Hall]] make his senior debut.<ref>{{Cite news|title=Chelsea hit five to cruise past Chesterfield|language=en-GB|work=BBC Sport|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/59911376|access-date=2022-01-11}}</ref> On 12 January, Chelsea beat Tottenham Hotspur 1–0 in the second leg of the Carabao Cup semi-final, booking a spot at [[Wembley Stadium|Wembley]] for the final. Antonio Rüdiger, who still had not signed a contract extension, scored the game's only goal.<ref>{{Cite news|title=Chelsea beat Spurs to reach EFL Cup final|language=en-GB|work=BBC Sport|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/59876396|access-date=2022-01-17}}</ref>

On 16 January, Chelsea took on league leaders Manchester City. The Citizens dominated the game for long periods, with [[Kevin De Bruyne]] scoring the game's only goal. Chelsea only managed one shot on target during the entire game, and the result saw Manchester City move 13 points clear at the top of the Premier League table.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Man City v Chelsea, 2021/22|url=https://www.premierleague.com/match/66556|access-date=2022-01-17|website=www.premierleague.com|language=en}}</ref> Two days later, Chelsea drew 1–1 with Brighton. The result meant that Chelsea had only won three of their last ten Premier League matches.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Brighton v Chelsea, 2021/22|url=https://www.premierleague.com/match/66573|access-date=2022-01-20|website=www.premierleague.com|language=en}}</ref> Following the match, Tuchel spoke about Chelsea's poor league form, saying "We were mentally tired and physically tired."<ref>{{Cite web|date=2022-01-18|title=Thomas Tuchel to give tired Chelsea players a break after Brighton draw|url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2022/jan/18/thomas-tuchel-to-give-tired-chelsea-players-a-break-after-brighton-draw|access-date=2022-01-20|website=The Guardian|language=en}}</ref>

Chelsea returned to winning ways on 23 January with a 2–0 win against Tottenham Hotspur in the Premier League. Hakim Ziyech opened the scoring with a curling left-footed shot from outside of the penalty area that arched into the top corner of the net.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Chelsea v Spurs, 2021/22|url=https://www.premierleague.com/match/66564|access-date=2022-01-23|website=www.premierleague.com|language=en}}</ref> The win meant that Chelsea had beaten Tottenham three times in the space of a month—the last Premier League team to achieve this feat was Aston Villa against [[Blackburn Rovers F.C.|Blackburn Rovers]] in January 2010.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Chelsea vs Tottenham: Premier League preview, team news, stats, predictions, kick-off time, live on Sky|url=https://www.skysports.com/football/news/11095/12521054/chelsea-vs-tottenham-premier-league-preview-team-news-stats-predictions-kick-off-time-live-on-sky|access-date=2022-01-23|website=Sky Sports|language=en}}</ref> Ziyech's goal was nominated for Premier League Goal of the Month for January, but it was awarded to Mateo Kovačić for his volley against Liverpool.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Kovacic volley voted Budweiser Goal of the Month|url=http://www.premierleague.com/news/2470108|access-date=2022-02-15|website=www.premierleague.com|date=4 February 2022 |language=en}}</ref>

=== February ===

Chelsea began February with a 2–1 win after extra time against [[Plymouth Argyle F.C.|Plymouth Argyle]] in the [[2021–22 FA Cup#Fourth round proper|FA Cup fourth round]] in a match led by assistant coach Arno Michels due to Tuchel's positive COVID-19 test. Marcos Alonso scored the match-winning goal in extra time and Kepa Arrizabalaga saved a late penalty to avoid a shootout.<ref>{{Cite news|title=Chelsea survive scare to beat Plymouth|language=en-GB|work=BBC Sport|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/60266346|access-date=2022-02-15}}</ref> Chelsea then travelled to the [[United Arab Emirates]] for the [[2021 FIFA Club World Cup|2021 Club World Cup]]. Chelsea faced Saudi side [[Al Hilal SFC|Al-Hilal]] in the semi-finals at the [[Mohammed bin Zayed Stadium]] in [[Abu Dhabi]] in a match they won 1–0 courtesy of a goal from Romelu Lukaku.<ref>{{Cite web|title=FIFA Club World Cup UAE 2021 Presented by Alibaba Cloud: Al Hilal SFC - Chelsea FC|url=https://www.fifa.com/tournaments/mens/clubworldcup/uae2021/match-center/origin1904-p.cxm.fifa.com/tournaments/mens/clubworldcup/uae2021/match-center/400213181|access-date=2022-02-15|website=www.fifa.com|language=en}}</ref> In the [[2021 FIFA Club World Cup Final|final]], Chelsea played Brazilian side [[Sociedade Esportiva Palmeiras|Palmeiras]] who beat [[Al Ahly SC|Al Ahly]] in the semi-finals. It was a tight contest, but Lukaku opened the scoring just after the second half began. However, Palmeiras equalised just nine minutes later from the penalty spot after Thiago Silva was penalised for a handball, sending the match into extra time. The score remained level until the 117th minute, when Chelsea were also awarded a penalty for a handball.<ref>{{Cite web|title=FIFA Club World Cup UAE 2021 Presented by Alibaba Cloud: Chelsea FC - SE Palmeiras|url=https://www.fifa.com/tournaments/mens/clubworldcup/uae2021/match-center/origin1904-p.cxm.fifa.com/tournaments/mens/clubworldcup/uae2021/match-center/400213182|access-date=2022-02-15|website=www.fifa.com|language=en|archive-date=6 January 2026|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260106061944/https://www.fifa.com/tournaments/mens/clubworldcup/uae2021/match-center/origin1904-p.cxm.fifa.com/tournaments/mens/clubworldcup/uae2021/match-center/400213182|url-status=dead}}</ref> César Azpilicueta picked up the ball and appeared to be set to take the decisive penalty, but after being mobbed by Palmeiras players, he passed it to Kai Havertz, who scored. After the match, Azpilicueta stated that "it was a tactic because I knew how they are, I knew they were coming for the penalty taker, so I took the ball."<ref>{{Cite web|title=Cesar Azpilicueta's quick thinking kept Kai Havertz cool from the spot|url=https://sports.yahoo.com/cesar-azpilicueta-quick-thinking-kept-101611929.html|access-date=2022-02-15|website=sports.yahoo.com|date=13 February 2022 |language=en-US}}</ref> Chelsea won the match 2–1, winning the Club World Cup for the first time in their history, thus making them the second English side after Liverpool to win the international treble of the UEFA Champions League, UEFA Super Cup and FIFA Club World Cup. Thiago Silva was named the tournament's best player, and Chelsea won the Fair Play Award.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Thiago Silva wins adidas Golden Ball as best player of UAE 2021|url=https://www.fifa.com/tournaments/mens/clubworldcup/uae2021/news/origin1904-p.cxm.fifa.comthiago-silva-wins-adidas-golden-ball|access-date=2022-02-15|website=www.fifa.com|language=en}}{{Dead link|date=July 2023 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref>

Chelsea returned to Premier League action on 19 February beating Crystal Palace 1–0 at [[Selhurst Park]] after Hakim Ziyech scored an 89th-minute winner.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Crystal Palace v Chelsea, 2021/22|url=https://www.premierleague.com/match/66595|access-date=2022-02-19|website=www.premierleague.com|language=en}}</ref> Three days later, Chelsea hosted their Champions League Round of 16 tie against Lille, winning 2–0 after goals from Kai Havertz, who replaced Lukaku in the starting lineup, and Christian Pulisic.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Chelsea-LOSC|url=https://www.uefa.com/uefachampionsleague/match/2033901--chelsea-vs-losc/|access-date=2022-02-23|website=[[UEFA]]|language=en}}</ref> On 26 February, Chelsea released a club statement in which owner [[Roman Abramovich]] announced that we was "giving trustees of Chelsea's charitable Foundation the stewardship and care of Chelsea FC."<ref>{{Cite web |title=Statement from Club Owner Roman Abramovich |url=https://www.chelseafc.com/en/news/2022/02/26/statement-from-club-owner-roman-abramovich |access-date=2022-02-26 |website=ChelseaFC}}</ref> The move came two days after the [[Russo-Ukrainian War|2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine]] and suggestions that the UK government should seize Abramovich's assets for his role in the Russian state.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2022-02-24 |title=Roman Abramovich linked to Russian state and 'corrupt activity', MP says |url=https://www.theguardian.com/world/2022/feb/24/roman-abramovich-linked-to-russian-state-and-corrupt-activity-mp-says |access-date=2022-02-26 |website=The Guardian |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=2022-02-24 |title=Leaked documents say Roman Abramovich paid for political influence, says Labour MP |url=https://www.independent.co.uk/news/uk/politics/roman-abramovich-russia-chelsea-bryant-b2022345.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220224174008/https://www.independent.co.uk/news/uk/politics/roman-abramovich-russia-chelsea-bryant-b2022345.html |archive-date=2022-02-24 |url-access=limited |url-status=live |access-date=2022-02-26 |website=The Independent |language=en}}</ref>

On 27 February, Chelsea played Liverpool in the [[2022 EFL Cup Final]]. The match was played at a quick pace, with both teams creating a number of high-quality chances. Mason Mount and Christian Pulisic both had opportunities to score in the first half, while Édouard Mendy made a series of important saves including one at point-blank range against [[Sadio Mané]]. The match went to extra time after [[Joël Matip|Joel Matip's]] close-range finish was ruled out for a foul. Chelsea also put the ball in the back of the net three times, but all were ruled offside.<ref name=":12">{{Cite news |title=Liverpool beat Chelsea on penalties |language=en-GB |work=BBC Sport |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/60450274 |access-date=2022-03-03}}</ref> The final of these goals saw a [[Romelu Lukaku]] goal narrowly ruled out for offside, with the Belgian forward's bicep being used to determine the line for offside. Despite many opportunities, neither team could break the deadlock after 120 minutes, so the match went to a penalty shootout. Thomas Tuchel substituted goalkeeper Édouard Mendy for Kepa Arrizabalaga, as he had done in the [[2021 UEFA Super Cup|Super Cup]]. Chelsea shot second, and after ten rounds of shots every player had scored leaving the two goalkeepers to shoot. Liverpool goalkeeper [[Caoimhín Kelleher|Caoimhin Kelleher]] dispatched his penalty before Arrizabalaga shot over the crossbar, meaning that Liverpool won the Carabao Cup 11–10 on penalties.<ref name=":12" /> It was the longest shootout in [[List of EFL Cup finals|EFL Cup Final]] history.<ref>{{Cite web |title=League Cup Winners - C.F. Classics |url=https://www.cfclassics.co/cups/england/leaguecup/english-league-cup-winners.htm |access-date=2022-03-03 |website=www.cfclassics.co}}</ref> After the game, [[Trevoh Chalobah]] openly criticised referee [[Stuart Attwell]] for failing to penalise a challenge from [[Naby Keïta]] which required stitches.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://metro.co.uk/2022/02/28/chelsea-defender-trevoh-chalobah-blasts-referee-over-naby-keita-tackle-16186517/|title=Chelsea defender Trevoh Chalobah blasts referee over Naby Keita tackle in Carabao Cup final|first=Chris|last=Davie|date=28 February 2022|access-date=28 February 2022|website=metro.co.uk}}</ref>

=== March ===

On 2 March, just hours before Chelsea took on [[Luton Town F.C.|Luton Town]] in the [[2021–22 FA Cup#Fifth round proper|FA Cup fifth round]], Roman Abramovich announced that he planned to sell the football club, stating "I have always taken decisions with the Club's best interest at heart. In the current situation, I have therefore taken the decision to sell the Club, as I believe this is in the best interest of the Club, the fans, the employees, as well as the Club's sponsors and partners."<ref name=":13">{{Cite web |title=Statement from Roman Abramovich  |url=https://www.chelseafc.com/en/news/2022/03/02/statement-from-roman-abramovich |access-date=2022-03-03 |website=ChelseaFC}}</ref> He also stated his intent to donate all proceeds of the sale to the victims of the [[2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine|war in Ukraine]].<ref name=":13" /> Chelsea went on to beat Luton Town 3–2 with goals from [[Saúl Ñíguez|Saúl]], [[Timo Werner]], and [[Romelu Lukaku]].<ref>{{Cite news |title=Lukaku hits winner as Chelsea beat Luton |language=en-GB |work=BBC Sport |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/60562803 |access-date=2022-03-03}}</ref> In the following days, numerous reports about interested buyers surfaced including Swiss billionaire [[Hansjörg Wyss]], [[Los Angeles Dodgers]] and [[Los Angeles Lakers|Lakers]] shareholder [[Todd Boehly]], Pakistani businessman [[Javed Afridi]], and other unnamed parties.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Hu |first=Krystal |date=2022-03-04 |title=Exclusive: Chelsea FC's banker says Abramovich's exit will not be rushed |language=en |work=Reuters |url=https://www.reuters.com/markets/europe/exclusive-chelsea-fcs-banker-says-abramovichs-exit-will-not-be-rushed-2022-03-04/ |access-date=2022-03-13}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=2022-03-03 |title=Pakistani businessman in race to buy Chelsea. Peshawar Zalmi, London Zalmi float as new names |url=https://theprint.in/go-to-pakistan/pakistani-businessman-in-race-to-buy-chelsea-peshawar-zalmi-london-zalmi-float-as-new-names/856723/ |access-date=2022-03-13 |website=ThePrint |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=2022-03-05 |title=Sources: Chelsea sale drawing rival U.S. bidders |url=https://www.espn.com/soccer/chelsea-engchelsea/story/4608804/chelsea-drawing-interest-from-at-least-10-credible-buyers-sources |access-date=2022-03-13 |website=ESPN.com |language=en}}</ref> On 9 March, it was reported that Abramovich had received multiple bids but none matched the £3 billion valuation.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2022-03-09 |title=Sources: No Chelsea bids match £3BN valuation |url=https://www.espn.com/soccer/chelsea-engchelsea/story/4612715/chelseas-roman-abramovich-receives-multiple-bidsnone-match-3bn-valuation-sources |access-date=2022-03-13 |website=ESPN.com |language=en}}</ref> However, on 10 March, the British government froze all of Roman Abramovich's assets due to his close personal ties with [[Vladimir Putin]], leaving Chelsea unable to sell tickets or merchandise, buy or sell players, and negotiate contracts.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Statement from Chelsea FC |url=https://www.chelseafc.com/en/news/2022/03/10/statement-from-chelsea-fc |access-date=2022-03-13 |website=ChelseaFC}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |last=Panja |first=Tariq |date=2022-03-10 |title=Britain Freezes Assets of Roman Abramovich, Creating Crisis at Chelsea |language=en-US |work=The New York Times |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2022/03/10/sports/soccer/abramovich-chelsea-sanctions.html |access-date=2022-03-13 |issn=0362-4331}}</ref> The UK government issued Chelsea a license that allowed the club to continue footballing activities, ensuring employees continued to be paid, and that season-ticket holders could continue to attend games.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Abramovich and Deripaska among 7 oligarchs targeted in estimated £15 billion sanction hit |url=https://www.gov.uk/government/news/abramovich-and-deripaska-among-seven-oligarchs-targeted-in-estimated-15bn-sanction-hit |access-date=2022-03-13 |website=GOV.UK |language=en}}</ref> Subsequently, [[Three UK]] and [[Hyundai Motor Company|Hyundai]] announced that they were terminating their sponsorship partnerships with Chelsea, which reportedly totaled up to £50 million per year.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2022-03-10 |title=Mobile phone company Three suspends Chelsea football shirt sponsorship |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2022/mar/10/mobile-phone-company-three-suspends-chelsea-shirt-sponsorship |access-date=2022-03-14 |website=The Guardian |language=en}}</ref> Sponsor [[Trivago]] and kit maker [[Nike, Inc.|Nike]], however, maintained their existing deals with the club.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Whitehead |first=Jacob |title=Chelsea training kit sponsor Trivago will continue deal and 'support the club' |url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/3510434/2022/03/11/chelsea-training-kit-sponsor-trivago-will-continue-deal-and-support-the-club/ |access-date=2022-03-14 |website=The Athletic |date=11 March 2022 |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Crafton |first=Adam |title=Nike to maintain Chelsea partnership deal amid Abramovich sanctions |url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/3510420/2022/03/11/nike-to-maintain-chelsea-partnership-deal-amid-abramovich-sanctions/ |access-date=2022-03-14 |website=The Athletic |language=en}}</ref> On 12 March, Chelsea's company credit cards were frozen, significantly limiting day-to-day spending but still allowing for matchday transportation costs lower than 20,000 per game.<ref name=":14">{{Cite web |first=Dominic |last=Fifield |title=Chelsea temporarily have company credit cards frozen after Roman Abramovich hit with sanctions |url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/3510426/2022/03/11/chelsea-temporarily-have-company-credit-cards-frozen-after-roman-abramovich-hit-with-sanctions/ |access-date=2022-03-14 |website=The Athletic |date=12 March 2022 |language=en}}</ref> It was reported that this left Chelsea unable to buy fuel for the team's bus.<ref name=":14" /> Technical director [[Petr Čech]] stated, "We have many questions, we don't have many answers but we are determined to concentrate on things we can control" and noted that the club was running "day-to-day."<ref>{{Cite web |last=Whitehead |first=Jacob |title=Chelsea being run 'day to day' following Abramovich sanctions — technical director Cech |url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/4181386/2022/03/13/chelsea-being-run-day-to-day-following-abramovich-sanctions-technical-director-cech/ |access-date=2022-03-14 |website=The Athletic |language=en}}</ref>

Meanwhile, Chelsea continued to fulfil their regular season matches, beating Norwich 3–1 away at [[Carrow Road]] and beating [[Burnley F.C.|Burnley]] 4–0 at [[Turf Moor]], headlined by a strike from Reece James that was nominated as March Premier League goal of the month.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Burnley v Chelsea, 2021/22 |url=https://www.premierleague.com/match/66613 |access-date=2022-04-22 |website=www.premierleague.com |language=en}}</ref><ref name=":16">{{Cite web |title=March 2022's Budweiser Goal of the Month contenders |url=http://www.premierleague.com/news/2540641 |access-date=2022-04-22 |website=www.premierleague.com |date=27 March 2022 |language=en}}</ref> The Blues also won 1–0 against [[Newcastle United F.C.|Newcastle]] at [[Stamford Bridge (stadium)|Stamford Bridge]] with a last minute winner from [[Kai Havertz]] that was also nominated for Premier League goal of the month.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Norwich v Chelsea, 2021/22 |url=https://www.premierleague.com/match/66638 |access-date=2022-03-14 |website=www.premierleague.com |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Chelsea v Newcastle, 2021/22 |url=https://www.premierleague.com/match/66625 |access-date=2022-03-14 |website=www.premierleague.com |language=en}}</ref><ref name=":16" /> Prior to their trip to Lille for the second leg of the Champions League Round of 16, Thomas Tuchel noted that there were doubts about whether the team would be able to travel, stating "My last information is we are getting a plane. So we can go by plane and come back by plane. If not, we'll go by train. If not, we'll go by bus. If not, I'll drive a seven-seater. Honestly, I will do it. You can mark my words, I will do to arrive there."<ref name=":15">{{Cite web |title='I will drive a seven-seater' - Tuchel has travel back-up plan if Chelsea can't fly to France for Champions League tie vs Lille|url=https://www.goal.com/en-us/news/drive-seven-seater-tuchel-travel-back-up-plan-chelsea-can-t/blt4ca6dac3b036f9b3 |access-date=2022-03-31 |website=www.goal.com}}</ref> He went on, "of course, organization-wise, there are some negotiations going on and talks, but it doesn't influence me. That's what I mean, we have brilliant guys who organize the travel and we have, in every department, such committed people that at the moment things feel pretty normal."<ref name=":15" />

Chelsea's off-the-pitch turmoil continued in the build-up to the FA Cup quarter-final against [[Middlesbrough F.C.|Middlesbrough]], when the UK government rejected Chelsea's request to sell additional away tickets.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Middlesbrough ticket update |url=https://www.chelseafc.com/en/news/2022/03/15/middlesbrough-ticket-update |access-date=2022-03-31 |website=ChelseaFC}}</ref> As a result, Chelsea lodged a request to play the match behind closed doors, which was subsequently withdrawn after an official rebuke from Middlesbrough.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2022-03-15 |title=Chelsea withdraw FA Cup 'no fans' request |url=https://www.espn.com/soccer/chelsea-engchelsea/story/4617251/chelsea-want-fa-cup-tie-at-middlesbrough-played-behind-closed-doors |access-date=2022-03-31 |website=ESPN.com |language=en}}</ref> Chelsea went on to win the match 2–0 after goals from Romelu Lukaku and Hakim Ziyech.<ref>{{Cite news |title=Chelsea reach FA Cup semi-finals |language=en-GB |work=BBC Sport |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/60698095 |access-date=2022-03-31}}</ref>

The deadline for new ownership groups to submit applications was set on March 18 by Raine Group, an American bank overseeing the process of Chelsea's sale.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Hall |first=Peter |date=2022-03-18 |title=Chelsea bidders assemble as deadline approaches |language=en |work=Reuters |url=https://www.reuters.com/lifestyle/sports/deadline-approaching-bidders-assemble-take-chelsea-abramovich-2022-03-18/ |access-date=2022-03-31}}</ref> In the following week, [[The Raine Group]] narrowed a shortlist to four bidders, eliminating bids led by Nick Candy, [[Woody Johnson]], Saudi Media Group, Aethel Partners, and Centricus.<ref>{{Cite magazine |last=Calcutt |first=Rob |title=Saudi Media Group Not Shortlisted by Raine Group for Chelsea Takeover |url=https://www.si.com/soccer/chelsea/news/saudi-media-group-not-shortlisted-by-raine-group-for-chelsea-takeover |access-date=2022-03-31 |magazine=Sports Illustrated |date=24 March 2022 |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Chelsea sale: Unsuccessful bidders being informed they are out of running to succeed Roman Abramovich as owner |url=https://www.skysports.com/football/news/11668/12574252/chelsea-sale-unsuccessful-bidders-being-informed-they-are-out-of-running-to-succeed-roman-abramovich-as-owner |access-date=2022-03-31 |website=Sky Sports |language=en}}</ref> The remaining bidders included groups led by the Ricketts family, [[Todd Boehly]], [[Martin Broughton|Sir Martin Broughton]], and [[Stephen Pagliuca]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=2022-03-25 |title=Ricketts bid included on shortlist of four to buy Chelsea despite fan backlash |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2022/mar/25/chelsea-sale-boehly-and-broughton-bids-make-shortlist-to-buy-club-roman-abramovich |access-date=2022-03-31 |website=The Guardian |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Chelsea takeover: Who is on the preferred bidders shortlist & what happens next? |url=https://www.goal.com/en/news/chelsea-takeover-shortlist-preferred-bidder-stage-what/blt3b6feeb315707b45 |access-date=2022-03-31 |website=www.goal.com}}</ref> However, Islamophobic comments from Joe Ricketts surfaced on social media, which led many Chelsea fans to demand that the Ricketts family bid be removed from consideration.<ref>{{Cite web |title=MEDIA DIGEST: Joe Ricketts's Racist Emails Leaked, CAIR-Chicago Responds |url=https://www.cairchicago.org/blog/2018/9/media-digest-joe-ricketts |access-date=2022-04-19 |website=CAIR-Chicago |date=6 February 2019 |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Madhani |first=Aamer |title=Cubs ownership faces backlash after patriarch's racist, Islamophobic emails leaked |url=https://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/2019/02/05/cubs-joe-ricketts-racists-emails-islamophobic-backlash/2782712002/ |access-date=2022-04-19 |website=USA TODAY |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=2019-02-06 |title=Chicago Cubs family patriarch's Islamophobic and right-wing emails leaked |url=https://www.independent.co.uk/news/world/americas/us-politics/joe-ricketts-emails-comments-chicago-cubs-family-muslim-a8766806.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190207025840/https://www.independent.co.uk/news/world/americas/us-politics/joe-ricketts-emails-comments-chicago-cubs-family-muslim-a8766806.html |archive-date=2019-02-07 |url-access=limited |url-status=live |access-date=2022-04-19 |website=The Independent |language=en}}</ref> Chelsea Supporters' Trust released a statement on March 25 stating "our concerns about their [the Ricketts family] ability to run an inclusive, successful club on behalf of our diverse supporter base around the world have not been allayed."<ref>{{Cite news |last=Hall |first=Peter |date=2022-03-25 |title=Ricketts bid added to shortlist for Chelsea takeover |language=en |work=Reuters |url=https://www.reuters.com/lifestyle/sports/broughton-consortium-says-it-is-shortlist-buy-chelsea-2022-03-25/ |access-date=2022-03-31}}</ref>

Despite off-the-pitch turmoil, Trevoh Chalobah and Kai Havertz were nominated for the Premier League player of the month for March and Thomas Tuchel was nominated as Premier League manager of the month.<ref>{{Cite web |title=March 2022's Barclays Manager of the Month candidates |url=http://www.premierleague.com/news/2540639 |access-date=2022-04-22 |website=www.premierleague.com |date=27 March 2022 |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=March 2022's EA SPORTS Player of the Month nominees |url=http://www.premierleague.com/news/2540638 |access-date=2022-04-22 |website=www.premierleague.com |date=27 March 2022 |language=en}}</ref>

=== April ===

Chelsea began the month of April with a 4–1 defeat at home to [[Brentford F.C.|Brentford]]. Antonio Rüdiger opened the scoring in the 48th minute with a strike from 35 yards that was nominated for April's Premier League Goal of the Month award.<ref>{{Cite web |title=April 2022's Budweiser Goal of the Month contenders |url=http://www.premierleague.com/news/2602154 |access-date=2022-05-22 |website=www.premierleague.com |date=7 May 2022 |language=en}}</ref> However, Brentford rallied with three goals in ten minutes before scoring a fourth just before the full-time whistle. It was the first time that Brentford had won at Stamford Bridge since 1939.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Chelsea v Brentford, 2021/22 |url=https://www.premierleague.com/match/66644 |access-date=2022-04-22 |website=www.premierleague.com |language=en}}</ref> On 6 April, Chelsea took on [[Real Madrid CF|Real Madrid]] in the first leg of the Champions League quarter-final at home. [[Karim Benzema]] scored two headers three minutes apart in the first half, putting Chelsea at an early disadvantage. However, Kai Havertz pulled a goal back just before half time to halve the deficit. Just after the break, Benzema completed his hat-trick after he picked off a loose pass by Édouard Mendy. Despite chances late in the match from substitute Romelu Lukaku, Chelsea went on to lose the match 3–1.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Chelsea-Real Madrid |url=https://www.uefa.com/uefachampionsleague/match/2034653--chelsea-vs-real-madrid/ |access-date=2022-04-22 |website=[[UEFA]] |language=en}}</ref> Before the second leg, Chelsea travelled to [[St Mary's Stadium|St. Mary's Stadium]] to take on Southampton, where they won 6–0 courtesy of braces from Timo Werner and Mason Mount and goals from Kai Havertz and Marcos Alonso. The result was Chelsea's second largest win of the season.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Southampton v Chelsea, 2021/22 |url=https://www.premierleague.com/match/66660 |access-date=2022-04-22 |website=www.premierleague.com |language=en}}</ref> On 12 April, Chelsea travelled to the [[Santiago Bernabéu Stadium|Santiago Bernabéu]] to take on Real Madrid. The match began with a high intensity from both sides, but it was Chelsea who scored first with a goal from Mason Mount in the 15th minute. Six minutes after half time, Antonio Rüdiger doubled Chelsea's lead with a powerful header off a corner kick, levelling the score on aggregate at 3–3. Chelsea then had a Marcos Alonso goal disallowed by VAR after he was adjudged to have handled the ball, but in the 75th minute, Timo Werner scored to make it 3–0 on the night and 4–3 on aggregate after dribbling past two Real Madrid defenders and calmly scoring past [[Thibaut Courtois]]. However, in the 80th minute, Real Madrid levelled on aggregate after [[Luka Modrić]] picked out [[Rodrygo]]. The match went on to extra time, where both sides had chances. However, the final goal of the match was scored by Karim Benzema, who capitalized on a series of defensive errors. The match ended in a 3–2 victory for Chelsea but a 5–4 defeat on aggregate. Following the match, Thomas Tuchel stated "Yes, it always [hurts to lose] but these are the kinds of defeats we can digest, because we left no regrets out there. We played how we wanted to play, we showed the quality and the character that this team has. We deserved to go through. It was not meant to be today, we were simply unlucky."<ref>{{Cite web |title=Real Madrid-Chelsea |url=https://www.uefa.com/uefachampionsleague/match/2034659--real-madrid-vs-chelsea/ |access-date=2022-04-22 |website=[[UEFA]] |language=en}}</ref>

On 15 April, it was announced that the Ricketts group had withdrawn their bid to takeover Chelsea, stating "The Ricketts-Griffin-Gilbert Group has decided, after careful consideration, not to submit a final bid for Chelsea FC. In the process of finalising their proposal, it became increasingly clear that certain issues could not be addressed given the unusual dynamics around the sales process. We have great admiration for Chelsea and its fans, and we wish the new owners well."<ref>{{Cite web |date=2022-04-15 |title=Chelsea takeover: Ricketts family's consortium withdraws from race |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2022/apr/15/chelsea-takeover-ricketts-family-consortium-withdraws-from-race |access-date=2022-04-22 |website=The Guardian |language=en}}</ref>

Chelsea returned to winning ways against Crystal Palace in a 2–0 victory at [[Wembley Stadium|Wembley]] in the [[2021–22 FA Cup#Semi-finals|FA Cup semi-final]] to book a spot in the final against Liverpool.<ref>{{Cite news |title=Chelsea beat Palace to set up Liverpool cup final |language=en-GB |work=BBC Sport |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/61119547 |access-date=2022-04-22}}</ref> They returned to Premier League action with a 4–2 defeat to Arsenal at home on 20 April, with several defensive errors proving costly as the Gunners won at Stamford Bridge for the second consecutive season.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Chelsea v Arsenal, 2021/22 |url=https://www.premierleague.com/match/66584 |access-date=2022-04-22 |website=www.premierleague.com |language=en}}</ref> The result meant that Chelsea had conceded 11 goals in their last 3 home matches in all competitions, making it their leakiest home defense record in three matches since 1989.<ref>{{Cite web |title=England - Chelsea FC - Results and fixtures - Soccerway |url=https://us.soccerway.com/teams/england/chelsea-football-club/661/matches/ |access-date=2022-04-22 |website=us.soccerway.com}}</ref> On 24 April, Chelsea beat West Ham 1–0 with a 90th-minute winner from Christian Pulisic and ended April four days later with a 1–1 draw against Manchester United, in which [[Cristiano Ronaldo]] equalized two minutes after Marcos Alonso opened the scoring.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Chelsea v West Ham, 2021/22 |url=https://www.premierleague.com/match/66676 |access-date=2022-05-09 |website=www.premierleague.com |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Man Utd v Chelsea, 2021/22|url=https://www.premierleague.com/match/66705 |access-date=2022-05-09 |website=www.premierleague.com |language=en}}</ref> During this period, it was widely reported that Antonio Rüdiger had agreed to join Real Madrid when his contract expired in the summer and would be leaving the club at the end of the season.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2022-04-25 |title=Real Madrid close to agreeing deal with Chelsea's Antonio Rüdiger |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2022/apr/25/real-madrid-deal-chelsea-antonio-rudiger-free-transfer |access-date=2022-05-09 |website=The Guardian |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |title=Real agree deal for Chelsea's Rudiger - Balague |language=en-GB |work=BBC Sport |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/61229181 |access-date=2022-05-09}}</ref>
