=== May ===

Chelsea began the month of May with a 1–0 defeat to relegation-threatened Everton at [[Goodison Park]], who were managed by former head coach and club legend [[Frank Lampard]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Everton v Chelsea, 2021/22 |url=https://www.premierleague.com/match/66683 |access-date=2022-05-09 |website=www.premierleague.com |language=en}}</ref> On 4 May, it was reported that the sale of Chelsea was being stalled because Roman Abramovich wanted to restructure the sale to regain the £1.5 billion he had loaned to the club.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Chelsea sale in doubt as Roman Abramovich attempts to restructure deal to regain his £1.5billion loan |url=https://www.skysports.com/football/news/11668/12604888/chelsea-sale-in-doubt-as-roman-abramovich-attempts-to-restructure-deal-to-regain-his-1-5billion-loan |access-date=2022-05-09 |website=Sky Sports |language=en }}</ref> One day later, however, Chelsea released an official statement clarifying that these reports were false and that all proceeds from the club's sale would be donated to charitable foundations.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Statement on behalf of Mr Abramovich |url=https://www.chelseafc.com/en/news/2022/05/05/statement-on-behalf-of-mr-abramovich |access-date=2022-05-09 |website=ChelseaFC}}</ref> It was also reported that [[Jim Ratcliffe|Sir Jim Ratcliffe]] submitted a late bid worth £4.25 billion to buy Chelsea but was rejected out of hand.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Chelsea takeover: Sir Jim Ratcliffe's £4.25 billion bid to buy club 'rejected out of hand' |url=https://www.skysports.com/football/news/11095/12605280/chelsea-takeover-sir-jim-ratcliffes-4-25-billion-bid-to-buy-club-rejected-out-of-hand |access-date=2022-05-09 |website=Sky Sports |language=en}}</ref> The sale of Chelsea officially proceeded on 6 May, as an ownership group led by [[Todd Boehly]], Clearlake Capital, Mark Walter, and [[Hansjörg Wyss]] acquired the club.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Club statement |url=https://www.chelseafc.com/en/news/2022/05/06/club-statement |access-date=2022-05-09 |website=ChelseaFC}}</ref> The first match of the new era came on 7 May in a home match against Wolves. Chelsea led 2–0 after Romelu Lukaku scored a brace, but were pegged back as Wolves scored twice in the final 20 minutes of the match to level the score at 2–2.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Chelsea v Wolves, 2021/22 |url=https://www.premierleague.com/match/66696 |access-date=2022-05-09 |website=www.premierleague.com |language=en}}</ref> The result left Chelsea just one point ahead of Arsenal in fourth.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Premier League Table, Form Guide & Season Archives |url=https://www.premierleague.com/tables?co=1&se=418&ha=-1 |access-date=2022-05-09 |website=www.premierleague.com |language=en}}</ref> Marcos Alonso was substituted from the match at half time, and it was reported that this was due to an altercation with Thomas Tuchel, who stated "Marcos was not injured, it was just a decision we made."<ref>{{Cite magazine |last=Debono |first=Matt |title=Inside Marcos Alonso & Thomas Tuchel's half-time Chelsea bust-up vs Wolves |url=https://www.si.com/soccer/chelsea/news/inside-marcos-alonso-thomas-tuchels-half-time-chelsea-bust-up-vs-wolves |access-date=2022-05-09 |magazine=Sports Illustrated |date=8 May 2022 |language=en}}</ref> It was rumored that Marcos Alonso wanted to push for a move to Barcelona in the summer and that teammates César Azpilicueta and Andreas Christensen could also move to [[Camp Nou]] on a free, as their contracts were set to expire in the summer.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2022-05-08 |title=LIVE Transfer Talk: Alonso, Azpilicueta set to follow Christensen to Barca |url=https://www.espn.co.uk/football/blog-transfer-talk/story/4660502/transfer-talk-chelseas-alonsoazpilicueta-set-to-follow-christensen-to-barcelona |access-date=2022-05-09 |website=ESPN.com |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=2022-03-03 |title=Sources: Barca close in on Christensen, Kessie |url=https://www.espn.co.uk/football/soccer-transfers/story/4607819/barcelona-in-advanced-talks-with-andreas-christensenfranck-kessie-on-free-transfers-sources |access-date=2022-05-09 |website=ESPN.com |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Brennan |first=Feargal |date=2022-05-07 |title=Barcelona agree contract terms with Cesar Azpilicueta |url=https://www.football-espana.net/2022/05/07/barcelona-agree-contract-terms-with-cesar-azpilicueta |access-date=2022-05-09 |website=Football España |language=en}}</ref>

Chelsea won for the first time in May by beating relegation-threatened [[Leeds United F.C.|Leeds]] 3–0 midweek before the [[2022 FA Cup Final|FA Cup Final]] against Liverpool.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Leeds v Chelsea, 2021/22|url=https://www.premierleague.com/match/66664 |access-date=2022-05-21 |website=www.premierleague.com |language=en}}</ref> The final took place on 14 May 2022 at [[Wembley Stadium|Wembley]] and was a repeat of the [[2022 EFL Cup Final|Carabao Cup Final]] earlier in the season. Chelsea lined up in their away yellow uninform, possibly due to a [[Superstition|superstitious belief]] that it would give them a better chance of winning.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Why are Chelsea wearing yellow kit in FA Cup final vs Liverpool & why isn't Havertz in the squad?|url=https://www.goal.com/en-us/news/why-are-chelsea-playing-fa-cup-final-against-liverpool-in-yellow-/blt60d1e14d07ee69e4 |access-date=2022-05-21 |website=www.goal.com}}</ref> Liverpool dominated early proceedings, but Chelsea were able to keep the Reds at bay with Édouard  Mendy called into action on several occasions. However, Chelsea grew into the game over the course of the first half, and Christian Pulisic and Marcos Alonso both had chances to score. In the second half, both sides continued to have chances, with Alonso hitting the crossbar and both [[Luis Díaz (footballer, born 1997)|Luis Díaz]] and [[Andrew Robertson]] hitting the post. The match finished scoreless at the end of ninety minutes, leading to an extra time which was bereft of major chances. Like the Carabao Cup Final, the match finished 0–0 and went to penalties. César Azpilicueta hit the post with an early penalty giving Liverpool the advantage. With the fifth kick of the shootout, [[Sadio Mané]] stepped up with a chance to score the decisive penalty but saw his shot saved by Mendy. However, in the seventh round of spot kicks, [[Alisson]] saved Mason Mount's penalty, and [[Kostas Tsimikas]] scored, winning the FA Cup Final for Liverpool. It was the second time of the season that Liverpool had beaten Chelsea in a cup final on penalties and was the third consecutive season in which Chelsea lost in the FA Cup Final.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2022-05-14 |title=Liverpool beat Chelsea on penalties in FA Cup final - as it happened |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/live/2022/may/14/chelsea-v-liverpool-fa-cup-final-live |access-date=2022-05-22 |website=The Guardian |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |first=Aimee |last=Lewis |title=Liverpool wins FA Cup final after beating Chelsea in nerve-racking penalty shootout |url=https://www.cnn.com/2022/05/14/football/chelsea-liverpool-fa-cup-final-spt-intl/index.html |access-date=2022-05-22 |website=CNN|date=14 May 2022 }}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |date=2022-05-13 |title=Liverpool beat Chelsea on penalties to win FA Cup final - recap |language=en-GB |work=BBC Sport |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/live/football/60919435 |access-date=2022-05-22}}</ref>

Following the disappointment in the Cup Final, Chelsea were boosted by the fact that [[Arsenal F.C.|Arsenal]] lost back-to-back matches against [[Tottenham Hotspur F.C.|Tottenham]] and [[Newcastle United F.C.|Newcastle]], guaranteeing them a top four finish and a spot in the [[2022–23 UEFA Champions League]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Chelsea's race for the Premier League top four - Champions League football secured|url=https://www.chelseafc.com/en/news/2022/05/03/chelsea-s-race-for-the-premier-league-top-four---four-games-to-g |access-date=2022-05-22 |website=ChelseaFC}}</ref> Chelsea then drew Leicester City 1–1 in their penultimate match of the season, which all but secured third place for the Blues due to their far superior goal difference to Tottenham.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Chelsea v Leicester, 2021/22|url=https://www.premierleague.com/match/66605 |access-date=2022-05-22 |website=www.premierleague.com |language=en}}</ref> On the final day of the season, Chelsea beat Watford 2–1 after [[Ross Barkley]] scored a stoppage time winner, confirming their third-place finish with 74 points, 19 points behind champions Manchester City.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Chelsea v Watford, 2021/22 |url=https://www.premierleague.com/match/66716 |access-date=2022-05-27 |website=www.premierleague.com |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Premier League Table, Form Guide & Season Archives |url=https://www.premierleague.com/tables?co=1&se=418&ha=-1 |access-date=2022-05-27 |website=www.premierleague.com |language=en}}</ref> Chelsea broke a new Premier League record by becoming the first side in the history of the competition not to be losing a match at half-time within a season.<ref>{{cite web |title=The 2021–22 Premier League Stats You Might Not Know |url=https://theanalyst.com/eu/2022/05/premier-league-stats-2021-22-quirky/ |website=The Analyst |date=23 May 2022}}</ref>

On 28 May, the club announced that a "final and definitive agreement" was entered to sell the club to the consortium of Boehly and Clearlake Capital.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Club statement {{!}} Official Site {{!}} Chelsea Football Club |url=https://www.chelseafc.com/en/news/2022/05/28/club-statement |access-date=2022-05-31 |website=ChelseaFC}}</ref> On 30 May, the club announced that the acquisition of the club to the said consortium had been completed.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Consortium led by Todd Boehly and Clearlake Capital completes acquisition of Chelsea Football Club {{!}} Official Site {{!}} Chelsea Football Club |url=https://www.chelseafc.com/en/news/2022/05/30/consortium-led-by-todd-boehly-and-clearlake-capital-completes-ac |access-date=2022-05-31 |website=ChelseaFC}}</ref> The sale of the club was approved by the UK and Portuguese Governments, the European Union and Premier League.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2022-05-24 |title=Prem approves Boehly-led Chelsea takeover |url=https://www.espn.com/soccer/chelsea-engchelsea/story/4674422/chelsea-takeover-premier-league-approves-todd-boehly-led-bid |access-date=2022-05-27 |website=ESPN.com |language=en}}</ref> Several players also officially announced their departures from Chelsea, including [[Danny Drinkwater]] and [[Antonio Rüdiger]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=2022-05-26 |title=Drinkwater says time at Chelsea was 'business move gone wrong' as he says sorry to fans |url=https://talksport.com/football/1118807/danny-drinkwater-apologises-chelsea-fans-departure/ |access-date=2022-05-27 |website=talkSPORT |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=2022-05-20 |title=Dear Chelsea|first=Antonio |last=Rüdiger |url=https://www.theplayerstribune.com/posts/antonio-ruediger-chelsea-fc-soccer-premier-league |access-date=2022-05-27 |website=The Players' Tribune |language=en-US}}</ref>

== Players ==

== Pre-season and friendlies ==
On July 14, Chelsea announced they would visit [[EFL Championship|Championship]] side [[AFC Bournemouth|Bournemouth]] on 27 July for a pre-season friendly.<ref>{{cite news |title=Bournemouth Pre-Season Game Announced |url=https://www.chelseafc.com/en/news/2021/07/14/bournemouth-pre-season-game-announced?cardIndex=0-0 |publisher=Chelsea F.C. |access-date=14 July 2021}}</ref> Prior to this, they would face [[Peterborough United F.C.|Peterborough United]] in a behind-closed-doors friendly at their [[Cobham Training Centre]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.peterboroughtoday.co.uk/sport/football/peterborough-united/peterborough-united-manager-excited-to-see-how-his-side-fare-at-chelsea-3306563|title=Peterborough United manager excited to see how his side fare at Chelsea|newspaper=Peterborough Telegraph |date=13 July 2021|access-date=17 July 2021|publisher=Peterborough United F.C.}}</ref>

=== FA Cup ===
{{Main|2021–22 FA Cup}}
Chelsea were drawn at home to [[Chesterfield F.C.|Chesterfield]] in the third round.<ref>{{cite news |title=Third round Draw |url=https://www.thefa.com/news/2021/dec/06/emirates-fa-cup-third-round-proper-draw-20210612 |date=6 December 2021 |publisher=The Football Association |access-date=9 December 2021}}</ref> In the fourth round, Chelsea were drawn at home to [[Plymouth Argyle F.C.|Plymouth Argyle]].<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.thefa.com/news/2022/jan/09/emirates-fa-cup-fourth-round-proper-draw-20220901 |title=The Draw for the fourth round proper of the Emirates FA Cup has been Made |date=9 January 2022 |access-date= 9 January 2022 |publisher=The Football Association}}</ref> They were drawn away to [[Luton Town F.C.|Luton Town]] in the fifth round.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/60279913|title=FA Cup fifth-round draw: Peterborough host Man City, Luton v Chelsea, Middlesbrough v Tottenham|publisher=BBC Sport|date=6 February 2022|access-date=6 February 2022}}</ref> In the quarter-finals, Chelsea were drawn away to [[Middlesbrough F.C.|Middlesbrough]].<ref>{{Cite tweet |user=EmiratesFACup |number=1499473871216553989 |author=Emirates FA Cup |title=The draw for the quarter-finals of the #EmiratesFACup has been made! What game are you most excited for? |language=en |date=3 March 2022}}</ref>

=== EFL Cup ===
{{Main|2021–22 EFL Cup}}

Chelsea entered the competition in the third round, due to participation in [[UEFA competitions]], and were drawn at home to [[Aston Villa F.C.|Aston Villa]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Carabao Cup Round Three draw confirmed |url=https://www.efl.com/news/2021/august/carabao-cup-round-three-draw-confirmed/ |publisher=EFL |access-date=26 August 2021}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Carabao Cup third round Date Confirmed |url=https://www.chelseafc.com/en/news/2021/08/27/carabao-cup-third-round-date-confirmed?cardIndex=0-1 |publisher=Chelsea F.C. |access-date=27 August 2021}}</ref> In the fourth round they were again drawn at home, against [[Southampton F.C.|Southampton]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Carabao Cup Round Four draw: confirmed ties |url=https://www.efl.com/news/2021/september/carabao-cup-round-four-draw-confirmed-ties/ |publisher=English Football League |access-date=23 September 2021}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |title=Carabao Cup Date Confirmed |url=https://www.chelseafc.com/en/news/2021/09/24/carabao-cup-date-confirmed?cardIndex=0-3 |access-date=24 September 2021 |publisher=Chelsea F.C. |date=24 September 2021}}</ref>
